## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Recent refactoring PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/37232 created a serious issue with the Influx sensor. The test query to determine connectivity with Influx V1 was `SHOW SERIES LIMIT 1;`. I thought that this query was one that worked with or without a database specified and thus could just be used to determine connectivity with the server, similar to how `buckets()` is used with V2 Influx. This is incorrect, database is not optional. Therefore when used during initial setup to test connectivity outside of the context of any particular sensor this can break.

This PR simply changes the query to `SHOW DATABASES;` which does work in this context. It always returns the list of databases the currently authenticated user can see based on privileges. Will follow this up with another PR to use this info to validate the sensors are pointing to valid databases/buckets but for now just fixing the introduced bug.

   host: <HOST>

review_comments: Did we have a test query for the sensor platform before the refactor?

Yes. `SHOW SERIES LIMIT 1;` was the one that was there. The reason it worked before is because each sensor has its own `InfluxDBClient` instance and so each did its own test on creation of the sensor. Since each sensor has a database this was all fine.

But one of the things I did in the refactor was change it so the same `InfluxDBClient` instance is shared among all sensors. This meant I had to do the test before the sensors are setup. Which means I don't necessarily know what bucket/database to connect to, the user may have configured that per sensor (like what happened in the linked issue). So I need a test that can be run just against Influx itself and not against any particular database.

Note that I also think in the end this new query will be an improvement. I am already working on adding back in the logic that only sets up sensors pointing to a bucket/database the user can see. Now with this query I can do that with only the output of a single query whereas before it was doing one query per sensor for that check.

Sounds good!

This test query has changed two times over the years. First change was due to too heavy query and second change was due to admin permissions required. How does `SHOW DATABASES` measure in that regard?

Yea I was worried about that and I actually think this is the ideal one in this spot. I was looking up how Influx handles permissions and it says specifically that non-admin users can do a `SHOW DATABASES` to see the databases they have READ and/or WRITE permissions on. So not only does that make it a good connectivity test in this spot, I can actually use the output to validate the database(s) listed on queries since it says it will only return the DBs the user can see.

Here's the doc for reference: https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v1.8/administration/authentication_and_authorization/#non-admin-users

Oh and your second question, its very very light.  It literally just returns a dictionary with one field per database the user can see. It looks like this against my testing V1 instance:
```
>>> list(influx.query("SHOW DATABASES;").get_points())
[{'name': '_internal'}, {'name': 'Test'}, {'name': 'AnotherDB'}]
```
